section: SC/ST rights - Articles 15, 16, 17, 46, 164, 244, 330, 332, 335; abolition of untouchability
subsections: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s: Under Article 35(a)(ii) of the Constitution of India, the power to prescribe punishment for offences under Article 17 belongs to
o: Both Parliament and State Legislatures concurrently
accepted.x: Article 35(a)(ii) gives Parliament, and not the State Legislatures, the power to prescribe punishment for offences relating to Article 17.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority would do this job, while distinguishing Parliament from State Legislatures.
accepted.sec: Article 17 - abolition of untouchability

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the application of Article 17:
1. Article 17 binds private persons as well as the State.
2. The State is required to act against private persons who practise untouchability.
3. Article 17 applies only to acts committed by public servants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Article 17 has horizontal application and binds private persons as well as the State. It is not confined to acts of public servants.
accepted.tq: Split the options by identifying the statement that wrongly narrows a Fundamental Right to the State alone.
accepted.sec: Article 17 - abolition of untouchability

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the term “untouchability” in the constitutional context?
o: It is exhaustively defined in Article 17.
It is defined in the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1976.
It is defined only in the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
Neither the Constitution nor any law defines the term.
accepted.x: Neither the Constitution nor any law provides a definition of “untouchability”. Its meaning has been developed through judicial interpretation.
accepted.tq: Test the exact legal position against plausible but over-specific statutory definitions.
accepted.sec: Article 17 - abolition of untouchability

accepted.s: The Mysore High Court interpreted “untouchability” under Article 17 as referring to
o: its literal meaning in ordinary language
accepted.x: The Mysore High Court held that Article 17 covers untouchability as historically developed, rather than the literal meaning of the word.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the literal meaning and the judicially accepted historical meaning.
accepted.sec: Article 17 - abolition of untouchability

accepted.s: Which one of the following is excluded from the scope of “untouchability” as interpreted by the Mysore High Court?
o: Residential segregation based on caste practice
Social boycott of a few individuals
Denial of entry into a temple on grounds of untouchability
Denial of access to a public water source
accepted.x: The judicial interpretation excludes the social boycott of a few individuals from the meaning of untouchability under Article 17.
accepted.tq: Find the exception by separating historically developed untouchability practices from an isolated social boycott.
accepted.sec: Article 17 - abolition of untouchability

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an offence covered by the Protection of Civil Rights law in relation to untouchability?
o: Providing reservation in public employment to an eligible Scheduled Caste candidate
Denying access to shops, hotels and places of entertainment
Barring entry to a place of public worship
Justifying untouchability on religious or traditional grounds
accepted.x: The Protection of Civil Rights law covers practices such as denial of temple entry, justification of untouchability and denial of access to public facilities. Providing reservation in public employment is not one of the listed offences.
accepted.tq: Find the item outside the statutory list rather than choosing a familiar Scheduled Caste-related provision.
accepted.sec: Article 17 - abolition of untouchability

accepted.s: Section 7(1)(d) of the Protection of Civil Rights law deals with insulting a member of a Scheduled Caste
o: on the ground of language alone
accepted.x: Section 7(1)(d) concerns insulting an SC member on the ground of untouchability.
accepted.tq: Match the statutory provision with its precise ground instead of a neighbouring discrimination ground.
accepted.sec: Article 17 - abolition of untouchability

accepted.s: Which one of the following does NOT represent a form of untouchability mentioned in the constitutional context?
o: The two-tumbler system in tea shops
Election of representatives through universal adult franchise
accepted.x: The two-tumbler system, denial of temple entry and residential segregation are listed forms of untouchability. Universal adult franchise is unrelated to such a practice.
accepted.tq: Identify the odd item by grouping concrete discriminatory practices together.
accepted.sec: Article 17 - abolition of untouchability

accepted.s: A conviction for an offence relating to untouchability results in disqualification from contesting elections under
o: Section 7 of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1976
Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
accepted.x: Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides disqualification from contesting elections upon conviction for untouchability offences.
accepted.tq: Match the consequence with the correct statutory source, not with the constitutional article governing reservation.
accepted.sec: Article 17 - abolition of untouchability

accepted.s: The concept of “structural violence”, in the context of untouchability, refers to
o: violence caused exclusively by international conflict
violence committed only by armed forces
accepted.x: Structural violence is harm built into social structures. The concept is associated with Johan Galtung.
accepted.tq: Choose the precise conceptual definition rather than a literal or unrelated form of violence.
accepted.sec: Article 17 - abolition of untouchability

accepted.s: The two principal angles from which untouchability may be understood are
o: ritual pollution attached to people and practices used by society to protect itself from it
accepted.x: Untouchability involves both the stigma of ritual pollution attached to people and the practices adopted by the rest of society to protect itself from that supposed pollution.
accepted.tq: Recall the paired analytical dimensions rather than selecting broad social issues.
accepted.sec: Article 17 - abolition of untouchability

accepted.s: Before the constitutional change that altered the arrangement under Article 164(1), the States specifically requiring a tribal welfare Minister were
accepted.x: The original arrangement covered Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha. Bihar was later removed, while Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh were added.
accepted.tq: Use the time qualifier “originally” to distinguish the earlier list from the present list.
accepted.sec: Article 164(1) proviso - Tribal Welfare Minister

accepted.s: The 94th Constitutional Amendment resulted in which of the following changes relating to the tribal welfare Minister?
o: It removed Bihar and added Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh.
It added Bihar and removed Madhya Pradesh.
It removed Odisha and added Bihar and Rajasthan.
It abolished the office of the tribal welfare Minister.
accepted.x: The 94th Amendment, 2006, freed Bihar from the requirement and added Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh. Madhya Pradesh and Odisha continued in the list.
accepted.tq: Track the entries removed and added instead of confusing the amendment with abolition of the office.
accepted.sec: Article 164(1) proviso - Tribal Welfare Minister

accepted.s:
With reference to reservation of seats for SCs and STs in legislatures, consider the following statements:
1. The number of reserved seats is related to the population of the respective communities.
2. Separate electorates are provided for SC and ST voters.
3. All voters in the constituency elect the representative.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Reserved seats are provided in proportion to population, but there are no separate electorates. All voters in the constituency participate in electing the representative.
accepted.tq: Trap the reversal between reserved seats and separate electorates.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Constitutional Amendments in chronological order in relation to the extension of reservation of seats under Article 334:
A. 45th Amendment
B. 8th Amendment
C. 62nd Amendment
D. 23rd Amendment
accepted.x: The sequence is 8th Amendment (1959), 23rd (1969), 45th (1980) and 62nd (1989).
accepted.tq: Start with the amendment having the earliest year and verify the middle sequence.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s: Which Constitutional Amendment extended the reservation of seats under Article 334 up to 2030 and also ended the nomination of Anglo-Indians to legislatures?
accepted.x: The 104th Constitutional Amendment, 2019, extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs up to 2030 and ended Anglo-Indian nomination.
accepted.tq: Use the paired consequence—extension plus ending Anglo-Indian nomination—to identify the amendment.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s: The 51st Constitutional Amendment, 1984, provided for ST seats in the Lok Sabha for
o: Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram
accepted.x: The 51st Amendment, 1984, provided ST representation in the Lok Sabha for Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram.
accepted.tq: Test the exact four-State grouping and avoid substituting neighbouring north-eastern States.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s: The number of seats reserved for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha was refixed on the basis of the
o: 1971 Census and 1981 Census through the 42nd and 44th Amendments
1981 Census and 1991 Census through the 73rd and 74th Amendments
1991 Census and 2001 Census through the 84th and 87th Amendments
2001 Census and 2011 Census through the 87th and 91st Amendments
accepted.x: The 84th Amendment refixed the seat numbers on the basis of the 1991 Census, and the 87th Amendment did so on the basis of the 2001 Census.
accepted.tq: Match the Census years with the corresponding amendment numbers.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s: The total number of seats reserved for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha is stated as
accepted.x: The Lok Sabha has 84 seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and 47 seats reserved for Scheduled Tribes.
accepted.tq: Keep the category figures paired correctly; the distractors reverse or alter the two numbers.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
o: 7 SC seats and 29 ST seats out of 175
29 SC seats and 4 ST seats out of 175
29 SC seats and 7 ST seats out of 175
25 SC seats and 7 ST seats out of 175
accepted.x: In the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly, 29 seats are reserved for SCs and 7 for STs, out of 175 seats.
accepted.tq: Separate the Assembly figures from the Lok Sabha and Andhra Pradesh parliamentary figures.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the reserved seats for SCs and STs in Andhra Pradesh’s Lok Sabha representation?
o: 4 SC seats and 7 ST seats out of 25
1 SC seat and 4 ST seats out of 25
4 SC seats and 1 ST seat out of 25
29 SC seats and 7 ST seats out of 25
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has 4 Lok Sabha seats reserved for SCs and 1 seat reserved for STs, including Araku, out of 25 seats.
accepted.tq: Use the institution and total-seat denominator to avoid mixing parliamentary and Assembly figures.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Constitutional Amendment)
 a. 77th Amendment
 b. 81st Amendment
 c. 82nd Amendment
 d. 85th Amendment
List-II (Provision)
 i. Consequential seniority in promotion
 ii. Backlog vacancies as a separate class
 iii. Reservation in promotion under Article 16(4A)
 iv. Relaxation in qualifying marks for promotion
accepted.x: The 77th Amendment inserted Article 16(4A), the 81st dealt with backlog vacancies, the 82nd inserted the proviso to Article 335, and the 85th provided consequential seniority.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure amendment-purpose pair and eliminate codes with a misplaced provision.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s: The 77th Constitutional Amendment, 1995, inserted which provision?
o: The proviso to Article 335, relating to qualifying marks
Article 330, relating to Lok Sabha seats
Article 16(4A), relating to reservation in promotion
accepted.x: The 77th Amendment inserted Article 16(4A), enabling reservation in promotion for SCs and STs after the limitation of Article 16(4) to initial appointment.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the neighbouring 16(4A), 16(4B) and Article 335 amendments by their exact subject.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s: The 81st Constitutional Amendment, 2000, dealt with
o: extension of reservation under Article 334 to 2030
reservation of ST seats in the north-eastern States
backlog vacancies as a separate class outside the 50 per cent ceiling
accepted.x: The 81st Amendment inserted Article 16(4B), treating backlog vacancies as a separate class outside the 50 per cent ceiling.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact amendment-purpose pair instead of confusing it with the promotion and seniority amendments.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted the proviso to Article 335 permitting relaxation in qualifying marks or lowering of evaluation standards for promotion of SCs and STs?
accepted.x: The 82nd Amendment, 2000, inserted the proviso to Article 335 permitting such relaxation for SCs and STs in promotion.
accepted.tq: Use the exact Article 335 association to separate the 82nd Amendment from the Article 16 amendments.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s: The 85th Constitutional Amendment is associated with
o: relaxation in qualifying marks under Article 335
backlog vacancies being treated as a separate class
consequential seniority in promotion under Article 16(4A), with effect from 17 June 1995
reservation of seats for STs in the Lok Sabha
accepted.x: The 85th Amendment provided consequential seniority in promotion under Article 16(4A), with effect from 17 June 1995.
accepted.tq: Use the effective date and the phrase “consequential seniority” as the decisive identifiers.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding extensions under Article 334?
1. 8th Amendment — extension up to 1970
2. 45th Amendment — extension up to 1990
3. 79th Amendment — extension up to 2010
4. 95th Amendment — extension up to 2020
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct: the 8th Amendment extended the period to 1970, the 45th to 1990, the 79th to 2010 and the 95th to 2020.
accepted.tq: Verify each amendment-year endpoint pair before choosing the comprehensive code.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures

accepted.s: The successive extensions under Article 334 before the 104th Amendment were generally made for a period of
accepted.x: The extensions under Article 334 were made in periods of ten years each, from the 8th Amendment onwards.
accepted.tq: Test the recurring numerical pattern rather than memorising only individual amendment years.
accepted.sec: Reserved seats for SC/ST in legislatures
